evidence: The southern end of the Old Ghost Road starts at the Lyell Conservation Campsite (State Highway 6) in the Upper Buller Gorge, a 50 minute drive from Westport.
The northern end of the Old Ghost Road finishes at Seddonville, 50 km north of Westport on State Highway 67.
Follow the forgotten 19th century county dray road as it winds its way towards the Lyell Saddle (875 m).
Note that Goat Creek must be forded to reach the hut.

doubts: The northern end is given as Seddonville (T14), the place the text names; the road end feature F2 (where The Old Ghost Road meets Mokihinui Road) lies about 4 km east of that place and is not used. The southern start is the Lyell Conservation Campsite (T8). The Mōkihinui River South Branch confluence and the Mokihinui River gorge are passed through per the text's descriptions but are not separate features on the way. The Croesus stamping battery site is on tracks that branch off the trail; the text does not say it is a side trip, so it is not_on_route. Whether the huts are all passed is taken from the section headings and descriptions, all of which are on the main way.
